digest.component_or_area: code review criteria: tests and error-handling
propositions: A check deriving its pass/fail result from subprocess/file/network output or a grep/regex without verifying producer liveness cannot distinguish its verdict from the producer never running or emitting nothing

Nine instances of fail-open oracles appeared in a single session across test assertions (signal-killed child processes, colorized grep patterns, truncated logs) and shipped-code checks (unchecked return codes, silent lookup misses, pgrep self-matches)

The mirror defect (false alarming on absence) occurs when a broken instrument produces a confident failing result for a reason other than the condition it verifies, requiring the criterion to cover both pass and fail verdicts
Producer-liveness language must be added to the existing tests criterion (test-oracle population) and error-handling criterion (shipped-code population) rather than creating a new criterion
Calibration replay on 18 seeded cases (9 pre-fix, 9 post-fix) must validate that all pre-fix cases yield findings naming the fail-open defect and all post-fix cases remain silent
Documentation via rebar explain review must include two worked examples showing fail-open detection in test code and shipped code scenarios
